title: The excitement of making a sale.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
I just noticed I sold a copy of my plugin, which I can't link here unfortunately (since it is against the rules to link to a payed product) That is fine, because I don't want to talk about my plugin.
I want to talk about that sale... After all the bits and parts taken by tax and the platforms, I may have made $2 from that $5 sale. When I take a dump at work (during hours), I make more money. So why do I still get excited about a sale?
To sketch a full picture: I am close to hitting a $100 gross revenue. That means, I made less than $100 in total, ever since I started. And that is before all the bits and pieces are takes out by tax and platforms! This means I really make a sale once in a while. The money isn't really noticeable. So that isn't the reason I get excited when I see I made a sale...
If the money isn't the reason I get excited every time someone buys my plugin, then what is? Well, the reason I get excited when someone buys my plugin, is that someone thought my plugin was worth $5. Something I created, is going to be used to make something else that someone else creates more fabulous.
Do you have the same feeling when you make a sale? Not the excitement for the money, but for the fact that someone was willing to pay for something you created, I mean. And for those who make more then a few bucks per year, does this excitement go away when the sales go up?

posts.author: Timeline_man
posts.body:
I get excited for sales, but my revenue is also rather diverse in that way. I sell my game, art and music for said game, other artwork, and that's all also split between digital sales and the booths I do at events. I get a lot of joy from the idea of my work growing bigger than myself, but I
do
have the (some may say foolish) dream of being able to survive primarally off of my creations. Now, the One sale per 4 months on Itch probably isn't going to be that, but it is a set of eyes, a set of eyes that might come back someday, when I have more stuff.
there's also an existential aspect for me: If people unconnected to me have my works, they can share it with other people, and thus my work has a better chance to outlive me. That's one of the reasons why I started selling discs of my game at events.

posts.author: Indinera
posts.body:
I've gotten sales from my games every day for over 16 years so I don't really get excitement from it anymore. That said,
millions
of sales would be a different story

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
I don't charge for my plugins, the effort to pay ratio on selling plugins is too high to be worth doing for money. The plugins I make are solving my own problems or a problem I took an interest in and made a solution for as "charity" for the community, and a way of giving back.
I make a living selling things I didn't make myself because I can live off it. I rarely get appreciation for it so it is entirely for the money. If I didnt get paid for it I wouldnt do it.

posts.body:
I'm a simple guy
I like seeing number grow bigger.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Willibab said:
I'm a simple guy

Click to expand...
Well said, for a simple guy.
I couldn't have said it any better.
I just finally hit the $100 mark, as a total in all those years. That was amazing.
But I get also excited if one of my other projects, which are all free, get played a lot more today than yesterday. I don't get less excited just because those don't earn me money.
You know what I also find fascinating? Trying to find out where those sudden plays come from. Sometimes I have 2 or 3 days where a specific project, or all of my projects, suddenly get a lot of attention, while I haven't posted those or updated them for a while.
The stupid thing is: That gets me excited, so I want it to grow more. So I would suddenly share that old project again on facebook or here or something... But then the views seem to stop instead of expand.
It is like: When I put my plugin on sale for 50% off for a week and promote it a little, I don't get a single sale, and a few weeks after, 3 sales for full price. How? I literally never sold the plugin for less then full price... Well, I sold it for a 50% discount once, when the full price was $10, which I lowered later on... So they still played the same as full price is now.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
What I tried to say is: Sometimes the numbers go up, without a noticeable cause. When I try, it doesn't work. When I do nothing, I get all the clicks and downloads...
It is like trying to pick up a woman in a bar. When you try too hard, no woman wants to talk to you, but when you don't try at all and just have fun, you get their attention.

posts.body:

This is exactly my opinion. When you charge for a plugin, people expect you to offer free support for it forever, which is absolutely not reasonable for the price they accepted to pay. I really like the open-source business model where the code is free, but support is expensive.
And I guess that's one of the reasons so many successful script/plugin dev. disappear after some time.

Well yeah, if someone is charging for a plugin they should support it. If they're frequently getting questions on how to use it it's up to the dev to improve documentation. I think it's reasonable to turn down new feature requests but fixing bugs or anything that gets in the way of core functionality that was advertised should be expected.
Most RPG Maker users move on to other engines/hobbies/things in life, not just plugin devs.
